notes: Two different orderings that both couple conductivity to pH, stated in different files. The calibration sequence is A6.8: mp-calibration-order-08 (temperature, then specific conductance, pH, dissolved oxygen, ORP, turbidity, then ion-selective and fluorescence sensors), mp-ionic-strength-rationale-09 (the order runs from low to high ionic strength so residual standard cannot bias the next calibration), mp-triple-rinse-10 (three deionized-water rinses between standards), mp-calibrate-before-each-use-04, mp-bracket-standards-04, mp-a61-a67-definitive-06 (the per-parameter chapters remain definitive over A6.8's general guidance). The reason the conductivity-before-pH leg of that order is not optional is stated only in A6.3: sc-calibrate-sc-before-ph-01 — pH buffers and electrode filling solutions are high-ionic-strength contamination sources. Turn 2 asks about the physical order of probes in a flow-through cell, which is a different ordering entirely and is stated in A6.0 (fm-ph-downstream-of-conductivity-01) and A6.3 (sc-probe-upstream-of-ph-01, sc-flowcell-shield-sunlight-01), with A6.7 adjacent (a discrete turbidity sample must not be drawn from the flow-cell discharge). An A6.8-only answer gives the sequence with no rationale and misses the plumbing question; an A6.3-only answer has the pH constraint and not the full order. Predicted rag: nothing in the slice covers calibration order or flow-cell layout.

turns.content: New tech is doing his first sonde calibration. Does the order he does the sensors in actually matter, or can he just work through them however?

must_contain: states the order does matter and gives temperature first
gives specific conductance next, before pH
gives the remaining order as pH, then dissolved oxygen, then ORP, then turbidity, with ion-selective and fluorescence sensors last
explains the rationale as working from low to high ionic strength so residual standard cannot bias the next calibration
states specifically that conductivity must be calibrated before pH because pH buffers and electrode filling solutions are high in ionic strength and are a contamination source
states the sensors are rinsed three times with deionized water between different standards
states the sonde is calibrated or checked before each field use
must_not: invents a rinse count or a step not in the manuals
treats the general multiparameter chapter as replacing the per-parameter calibration chapters

turns.content: Same question for the flow cell we run at the well — does it matter which probe the water hits first once they're all plumbed in there?

must_contain: states the pH sensor is installed downstream of the conductivity sensor in the flow-through chamber
states the flow cell should be kept as close to the source water as possible and shielded from direct sunlight
notes the specific-conductance probe position relative to the pH electrode depends on the flow-cell design
must_not: repeats the calibration order as if it answered the plumbing question
invents a probe position rule not stated in the manuals
recommends drawing a discrete turbidity sample from the flow-cell discharge
